questions.q: Evaluate $\int 2x(x^2+1)^4\,dx$ using the substitution $u=x^2+1$.
questions.answer: $du=2x\,dx$. So $\int(x^2+1)^4\cdot2x\,dx=\int u^4\,du=\dfrac{u^5}{5}+C=\dfrac{(x^2+1)^5}{5}+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^3x\cos x\,dx$ using the substitution $u=\sin x$.
questions.answer: $du=\cos x\,dx$. When $x=0$, $u=0$; when $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $u=1$. $\int_0^1 u^3\,du=\left[\dfrac{u^4}{4}\right]_0^1=\dfrac{1}{4}$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x e^x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=x$, $dv=e^x\,dx$, so $du=dx$, $v=e^x$. $\int xe^x\,dx=xe^x-\int e^x\,dx=xe^x-e^x+C=(x-1)e^x+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x\ln x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=x\,dx$, so $du=\dfrac{1}{x}dx$, $v=\dfrac{x^2}{2}$. $\int x\ln x\,dx=\dfrac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\int\dfrac{x^2}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\,dx=\dfrac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\dfrac{x^2}{4}+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x^2e^x\,dx$, applying integration by parts twice.
questions.answer: First application: $u=x^2$, $dv=e^xdx$: $\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-\int2xe^x\,dx$. From the previous problem, $\int xe^x\,dx=(x-1)e^x+C$, so $\int2xe^x\,dx=2(x-1)e^x$. Result: $x^2e^x-2(x-1)e^x+C=(x^2-2x+2)e^x+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\cos^2x\,dx$ using the identity $\cos^2x=\dfrac{1+\cos2x}{2}$.
questions.answer: $\int\dfrac{1+\cos2x}{2}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x+\dfrac{\sin2x}{2}\right)+C=\dfrac{x}{2}+\dfrac{\sin2x}{4}+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\dfrac{1}{x^2-1}\,dx$ by first expressing the integrand in partial fractions.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{1}{x^2-1}=\dfrac{1}{(x-1)(x+1)}=\dfrac{A}{x-1}+\dfrac{B}{x+1}$. Solving: $A=\dfrac{1}{2}$, $B=-\dfrac{1}{2}$. $\int\left(\dfrac{1/2}{x-1}-\dfrac{1/2}{x+1}\right)dx=\dfrac{1}{2}\ln|x-1|-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln|x+1|+C=\dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left|\dfrac{x-1}{x+1}\right|+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int_1^e\dfrac{\ln x}{x}\,dx$, using the substitution $u=\ln x$.
questions.answer: $du=\dfrac{1}{x}dx$. When $x=1$, $u=0$; when $x=e$, $u=1$. $\int_0^1 u\,du=\left[\dfrac{u^2}{2}\right]_0^1=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int_0^{\pi}x\sin x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=x$, $dv=\sin x\,dx$, so $du=dx$, $v=-\cos x$. $\int x\sin x\,dx=-x\cos x+\int\cos x\,dx=-x\cos x+\sin x$. Evaluating from $0$ to $\pi$: $[-\pi\cos\pi+\sin\pi]-[0+0]=-\pi(-1)+0=\pi$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx$, and use it to evaluate $\int_0^1\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx$.
questions.answer: $\int\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx=\arctan x+C$. So $\int_0^1\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx=\arctan(1)-\arctan(0)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-0=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

sections.heading: Integration by substitution with trigonometric functions

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\sin^3x\,dx$, using the identity $\sin^2x=1-\cos^2x$ and the substitution $u=\cos x$.
questions.answer: Rewrite: $\sin^3x=\sin x(1-\cos^2x)$. Let $u=\cos x$, $du=-\sin x\,dx$. $\int\sin x(1-\cos^2x)\,dx=-\int(1-u^2)\,du=-u+\dfrac{u^3}{3}+C=-\cos x+\dfrac{\cos^3x}{3}+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\tan x\,dx$, using the substitution $u=\cos x$.
questions.answer: $\tan x=\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$. Let $u=\cos x$, $du=-\sin x\,dx$. $\int\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\,dx=-\int\dfrac{1}{u}\,du=-\ln|u|+C=-\ln|\cos x|+C=\ln|\sec x|+C$.

sections.heading: Integration by parts with a logarithmic integrand

questions.q: Evaluate $\int_1^e\ln x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=dx$, so $du=\dfrac{1}{x}dx$, $v=x$. $\int\ln x\,dx=x\ln x-\int x\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\,dx=x\ln x-x+C$. Evaluating from $1$ to $e$: $[e\ln e-e]-[1\ln1-1]=(e-e)-(0-1)=0+1=1$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\dfrac{1}{5+4\cos x}\,dx$ using the substitution $t=\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$, given that this substitution transforms $\cos x=\dfrac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}$ and $dx=\dfrac{2}{1+t^2}dt$, leading to the simplified integrand $\dfrac{2}{9+t^2}$.
questions.answer: Substituting: $\int\dfrac{1}{5+4\left(\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}\right)}\cdot\dfrac{2}{1+t^2}\,dt=\int\dfrac{2}{5(1+t^2)+4(1-t^2)}\,dt=\int\dfrac{2}{9+t^2}\,dt$. Using the standard result $\int\dfrac{1}{a^2+t^2}\,dt=\dfrac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\dfrac{t}{a}\right)+C$ with $a=3$: $2\cdot\dfrac{1}{3}\arctan\left(\dfrac{t}{3}\right)+C=\dfrac{2}{3}\arctan\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right)+C$.

sections.heading: Integration by parts with a trigonometric-exponential product

questions.q: Evaluate $\int e^x\cos x\,dx$, applying integration by parts twice and solving the resulting equation for the original integral.
questions.answer: Let $I=\int e^x\cos x\,dx$. First application: $u=\cos x$, $dv=e^xdx$, so $du=-\sin x\,dx$, $v=e^x$: $I=e^x\cos x+\int e^x\sin x\,dx$. Second application on $\int e^x\sin x\,dx$: $u=\sin x$, $dv=e^xdx$: $\int e^x\sin x\,dx=e^x\sin x-\int e^x\cos x\,dx=e^x\sin x-I$. Substituting back: $I=e^x\cos x+e^x\sin x-I$, so $2I=e^x(\cos x+\sin x)$, giving $I=\dfrac{e^x(\cos x+\sin x)}{2}+C$.

sections.heading: Finding the area between two curves using integration

questions.q: Find the area of the region enclosed between $y=\sin x$ and $y=\cos x$ for $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\leq x\leq\dfrac{5\pi}{4}$ (the interval on which $\sin x\geq\cos x$).
questions.answer: Area $=\int_{\pi/4}^{5\pi/4}(\sin x-\cos x)\,dx=\left[-\cos x-\sin x\right]_{\pi/4}^{5\pi/4}$. At $x=\dfrac{5\pi}{4}$: $-\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{4}-\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{4}=\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=\sqrt{2}$. At $x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$: $-\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}=-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=-\sqrt{2}$. Area $=\sqrt{2}-(-\sqrt{2})=2\sqrt{2}$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x^2\ln x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=x^2dx$, so $du=\dfrac{1}{x}dx$, $v=\dfrac{x^3}{3}$. $\int x^2\ln x\,dx=\dfrac{x^3}{3}\ln x-\int\dfrac{x^3}{3}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\,dx=\dfrac{x^3}{3}\ln x-\int\dfrac{x^2}{3}\,dx=\dfrac{x^3}{3}\ln x-\dfrac{x^3}{9}+C$.

questions.q: A particle's velocity is given by $v(t)=t\cos t$ metres per second. Find the particle's displacement over the interval $0\leq t\leq\pi$, using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Displacement $=\int_0^{\pi}t\cos t\,dt$. Using integration by parts with $u=t$, $dv=\cos t\,dt$, so $du=dt$, $v=\sin t$: $\int t\cos t\,dt=t\sin t-\int\sin t\,dt=t\sin t+\cos t+C$. Evaluating from $0$ to $\pi$: $[\pi\sin\pi+\cos\pi]-[0\sin0+\cos0]=[0-1]-[0+1]=-1-1=-2$. Displacement $=-2$ metres.

questions.q: This question has three parts. (a) Use the substitution $u=x^2+4$ to find $\int\dfrac{x}{x^2+4}\,dx$. (b) Use integration by parts to find $\int\arctan x\,dx$. (c) Hence, using the result of part (b) and the standard result $\int\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}dx=\arctan x+C$, evaluate $\int_0^1\arctan x\,dx$, giving an exact answer in terms of $\pi$ and $\ln$.
questions.answer: (a) $u=x^2+4$, $du=2x\,dx$: $\int\dfrac{x}{x^2+4}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{2}\int\dfrac{1}{u}\,du=\dfrac{1}{2}\ln|x^2+4|+C$. (b) Let $u=\arctan x$, $dv=dx$, so $du=\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}dx$, $v=x$: $\int\arctan x\,dx=x\arctan x-\int\dfrac{x}{1+x^2}\,dx=x\arctan x-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1+x^2)+C$ (using the result from part (a), with $4$ replaced by $1$). (c) Evaluating from $0$ to $1$: $\left[1\cdot\arctan1-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln2\right]-\left[0-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln1\right]=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln2$.

questions.q: Given the reduction formula $I_n=\int x^ne^x\,dx=x^ne^x-nI_{n-1}$ (obtained via integration by parts), and that $I_0=e^x+C$, use it to find $I_2=\int x^2e^x\,dx$.
questions.answer: $I_1=x^1e^x-1\cdot I_0=xe^x-e^x$ (ignoring the constant until the final step). $I_2=x^2e^x-2I_1=x^2e^x-2(xe^x-e^x)=x^2e^x-2xe^x+2e^x+C=(x^2-2x+2)e^x+C$, matching the result found earlier in this worksheet by direct repeated integration by parts.
